questions.q: What is the recommended core setup for a trustworthy upgrade test?
options: Test only the system databases, since user databases are unaffected by upgrades
Restore an actual, current production backup to a staging instance running the target version, then run the real application workload against it
Create a fresh empty database on the new version and run a few sample queries
Skip testing entirely if the upgrade is only a Cumulative Update
questions.explain: Real production data and a real workload surface data-skew, fragmentation, and scale issues that a fresh test database with sample rows would never reveal.

questions.q: What does Query Store provide that makes upgrade regression testing concrete rather than vague?
options: A Regressed Queries report ranking queries by performance change, with the old and new execution plans shown side by side
A guarantee that no query will ever regress after an upgrade
Automatic rollback of any query that runs slower after an upgrade
A replacement for taking backups before an upgrade
questions.explain: Query Store records historical plans and runtime stats, letting you directly compare before and after an upgrade via its Regressed Queries report.

questions.q: If Query Store reveals a specific query regressed after a test upgrade, what stopgap procedure can force it back to its prior plan?
options: sp_helpdb
DBCC CHECKDB
ALTER DATABASE SET COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL
sp_query_store_force_plan
questions.explain: sp_query_store_force_plan can force a specific historical plan for a query as a temporary fix while the underlying cause is investigated.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does 'passing' an upgrade test actually require?
options: Successfully restoring the backup, regardless of application behavior afterward
The new version number appearing correctly in @@VERSION
The application functions correctly end-to-end, no query shows an unacceptable regression in Query Store, and flagged breaking changes are addressed
The installer completing without throwing an error
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states that 'it installed without errors' is the bare minimum, not a passing test — passing requires measured application and query behavior.

questions.q: Why is a fresh, empty database with a handful of sample queries an inadequate upgrade test?
options: SQL Server refuses to run on a database with fewer than a minimum row count
Sample queries always run faster than real production queries, hiding no issues
It won't surface data-skew, fragmentation, or scale/concurrency issues that only appear with real production data and workload
Empty databases cannot be restored on a new SQL Server version
questions.explain: Realistic data distributions, index fragmentation, and production-scale volume and concurrency are exactly what surface optimizer and plan-related upgrade problems.
